3: The chat-first prior authorization prototype that PatientGPT is being built
4: from: a ChatGPT-shaped workspace for Advanced Spine & Orthopedics where
5: patients sit where projects would and each case is a conversation. This folder
6: is the design reference for the web app, the Tauri desktop app and the Flutter
7: mobile app. Everything in it is synthetic.
8: 
9: ## What is here
10: 
11: | File | What it is |
12: |---|---|
13: | `patient-chat-storyboard.html` | The guide: seven cases to work and each navigation click with the screen it produces. Published as the site's index page. |
14: | `patient-chat.html` | PatientGPT itself. Open it in a browser; it needs no server. File names keep the original `patient-chat` prefix so published links stay valid; the product name shown everywhere is PatientGPT. |
15: | `patient-chat/` | Its styles and scripts (see below). |
16: | `patient-chat-og.png` | The prototype's home screen, 1200×630, used as the link-preview image. |
17: | `publish-ipfs.sh` | Publishes this folder to the IPFS node under the IPNS name `pa-workbench-chat`. |
18: | `data-model.md` | The proposed PatientGPT data model: what it adds over the workbench schema, what it derives, and what it never stores. Read it before building. |
19: | `schema/patient-gpt.sql` | PostgreSQL DDL for that model, applied after the workbench `aso` schema; loads cleanly against `docs/design/schema/schema.sql` + `schema-ai.sql`. |
20: | `brand/` | The PatientGPT mark, "Spine in conversation" (chosen 4 October 2026): `icon.svg`, `mark.svg`, `mark-dark.svg`, `favicon.svg`, `wordmark-light.svg`, `wordmark-dark.svg`, raster `exports/` (1024, 180, 192, 512, favicon 32/16 and `.ico`), and `brand/patientgpt-brand-board.html`, the brand board that shows the mark in every application surface with its rules. The three concepts it was chosen from stay under `brand/concepts/`. |

25: ## How the prototype is put together
26: 
27: Classic scripts under one global, loaded in order from `patient-chat.html`.
28: Each file stays under about 500 lines.
29: 
30: | File | Owns |
31: |---|---|
32: | `tokens.css` | Design tokens, light and dark, borderless Flat 2.0 primitives, focus as a fill swap. |
33: | `shell.css`, `thread.css`, `surfaces.css`, `panel.css` | App shell, conversation, agent and surgeon surfaces, Files panel and viewers. |
34: | `ui.js` | DOM helpers, inline icon set, case state track, menus, dates. |
35: | `data.js`, `data-docs.js` | Synthetic patients and cases with one working record each; chart and policy documents. State, next move and blockers are derived from the record. |
36: | `agui-stream.js` | AG-UI-shaped event stream: run, step, tool call, streamed text, state delta (JSON Patch), interrupt, timestamp playback. |
37: | `a2ui-renderer.js` | Allowlisted A2UI-shaped surface renderer. Unknown components and actions are refused in place. |
38: | `conversations.js` | Conversations scoped to all patients, one patient or one case; seeded history. |
39: | `search.js`, `search-ui.js` | Simulated vector search over embedded case content. |
40: | `runs.js`, `runs-scope.js`, `flows.js` | The scripted agent: case runs, global and patient runs, per-case questions, attached-document handling, peer-to-peer, payer status. |
41: | `host-controls.js`, `records.js` | Surgeon-only controls drawn by the app (gates, signing, packet, call outcome) and the viewers for every generated record. |
42: | `files-panel.js`, `thread.js`, `composer.js`, `nav.js`, `shell.js` | Files and evidence panel, conversation drawing, composer, left navigation, routes and chrome. |
43: 
44: ## Rules the prototype holds
45: 
46: - A criterion changes only when a document is filed. A surgeon's answer is recorded as a statement, never as chart evidence.
47: - The agent never affirms a gate, signs, submits or records an outcome; those controls are drawn by the app for the signed-in surgeon.
48: - No approval odds. Reports run CASE, CRITERIA STATUS, CONFLICTS, BLOCKERS, NEXT MOVE. One question at a time.
49: - Met, gap and void always carry a label and a shape, never color alone.
